free_tier.stated: 10 GB on registration per the vendor's own App Store listing ('注册即享10GB，最高可扩至1TB'). The free download path is metered by wait rather than by bytes: a countdown, a captcha, and one file per 12 minutes, at no more than 50 KB/s.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published. The free path's real cap is one download per 12 minutes, which is a file count, not a size.

retention.stated: Not published on the vendor pages read. A third-party review states that a free user's files have no explicit term but may be cleared when they go more than 90 days without being downloaded, and that member files are kept permanently.

egress.terms: The vendor's VIP page states free downloads are capped at 不超过50KB/s (no more than 50 KB/s), with no 加速下载额度 (zero accelerated-download quota) for non-members.

interface_detail: Browser download with a captcha; the returned URL is fetchable by IDM or aria2, and multi-threading is the documented workaround for the single-thread cap.
tooling: Browser plus IDM/Xdown/Motrix. No API and no WebDAV.
chaining: The bottom of the Chinese retrieval economy: the host pays uploaders per download and taxes downloaders with waiting time, so a link here is worth only what a multi-threaded client can pull out of it.

limits.value: third-party reviews report 100-200 KB/s single-threaded; the vendor caps free downloads at 50 KB/s
one file per 12 minutes on the free path

limits_note: A third-party review also states that free users have a daily download-count limit, usually 10 per day; it is not reconciled with the per-file interval reported by the other source.

identity_cost.detail: The app requires an account to upload and to keep files; the first-party signup form offers registration by email, or by phone number with an SMS code, and a third-party review lists 微信 QR scan or QQ login. Downloading a shared file needs no account at all - that is the point of the model.

reliability_note: The payout model is the reliability risk: uploaders are paid 420 to 920 元 per 10,000 downloads depending on plan, so links are monetised and the host has an interest in keeping the free path slow.
confidence_note: The 10 GB figure is from the vendor's App Store listing. The 50 KB/s free cap is from the vendor's VIP page; the 100-200 KB/s range and the 12-minute interval are third-party measurements and are labelled as such. The landing page publishes no limits at all.

notes: Included because the 网赚网盘 model is what most Chinese share links point at once the mainstream pans throttle. The free tier is not a retrieval route here at any volume.
binding_note: At 50 KB/s the ceiling is 0.18 GB/hour, so 1 TiB of monthly transfer needs 5,700 hours of download time; the 12-minute interval makes it worse for many small files. The shaping is the wall, not any byte counter.
